metadata.note: The Poughkeepsie and Eastern line (Poughkeepsie - Stissing Junction - Pine Plains - Boston Corners - State Line, NY), drawn by operating company: Poughkeepsie and Eastern Railroad (opened 1871/1872; receiver 1874; sold 1875), Poughkeepsie, Hartford and Boston Railroad (15 May 1875 - 1886), and Poughkeepsie and Eastern Railway (13 Apr 1893 - merged into the Central New England 25 Jun 1907). Every span drawn is the research report's drawable: span. Research report: research/branches/poughkeepsie_and_eastern_railway.txt (status ready, researched 2026-10-19).
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4: features sharing geometry split at 15 May 1875 (P&E RR -> PH&B; drawn P&E RR to 1874, PH&B from 1875), 1 Apr 1884 (Boston Corners - State Line leg sold to the H&CW; PH&B trains thereafter end at Boston Corners), 22 Jan 1887 (PH&B -> New York and Massachusetts; NOT drawn) and 13 Apr 1893 (NY&M -> P&E Ry). NOT splits: the 1874 P&E RR receivership, the pre-1884 PH&B bankruptcy, the 1898 P&E Ry receivership, and Russell Sage's control of the P&E Ry. Colours: none of these companies had a colour in data/. The Poughkeepsie and Eastern RAILROAD (1866-1875) and the Poughkeepsie and Eastern RAILWAY (1893-1907) are SEPARATE CORPORATIONS that share the display name 'Poughkeepsie and Eastern'; on the maintainer's decision they carry one company string and ONE colour (#B6548E), with the legal name in each feature's company_legal. The PH&B has its own colour (#7AA725). Both hexes were chosen programmatically: used by no company in data/, and more than 30 CIELAB units from the CNE, NYNH&H, D&C, ND&C, R&C, H&CW, CNE&W and PR&NE colours on adjacent or shared track.

PH&B 1886 and the PH&B on Boston Corners - State Line in any year but 1881: withheld, not disproven.

Poughkeepsie riverfront / dock track (the Commons line's first 1.1 mi, to the reversal at (-73.92775, 41.72794)) and the Smith Street corridor north of the yard: very probably freight/dock track; not drawn (Rule 1).

Central New England era of the ex-P&E (block [7]): belongs to central_new_england_railway.geojson. Gaps noted for that file's owner: Poughkeepsie - Salt Point - Stissing - Pine Plains undrawn 1908-1911; the P&E's own Poughkeepsie - Salt Point alignment never drawn in the CNE era; Pine Plains - Ancram Lead Mines - Boston Corners drawn by no CNE feature.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] end, phb-poughkeepsie-boston-corners: 1885 is the last confirmed PH&B passenger year; 1886 withheld.

[OPEN] end, pe-poughkeepsie-boston-corners: 1904 is the last confirmed P&E Ry passenger year; 1905 - Jun 1907 withheld. The NY Public Service Commission (2nd District) 1907/1908 reports would likely settle it.

[ANCHOR] phb-boston-corners-state-line 1881: the only year a PH&B train is shown at the State Line / Millerton end, and its route over the Mount Riga leg is inferred. Whether PH&B trains regularly ran through to State Line 1875-1883 is unresolved.
NY&M 1887-1892: no passenger year confirmed (NY Railroad Commissioners' reports, Poor's Manual, Haight not reached).
Poughkeepsie passenger station position on the Smith Street corridor not checked against Sanborn 1895 sheet 32 or Beers 1891; the start point is fixed by fit to Fowler's mileage.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout.

properties.geometry_quality: Poughkeepsie (Smith Street) - Stissing Jct: traced 21.5 mi against 21.3 mi documented (Fowler NY line 12, Poughkeepsie (PE) 112.0 - Stissing Jn 90.7; WPE 21.11 mi on the post-1910 P&C entry). Routing before simplification: Commons:Poughkeepsie and Eastern Railway 12.7 mi, OSM:Poughkeepsie and Eastern Railway 8.8 mi, (connector) 0.0 mi. No straight-line leg. Poughkeepsie end: the Commons line begins at the Hudson riverfront (-73.93694, 41.71384), runs north-east 1.1 mi to a reversal at (-73.92775, 41.72794), then doubles back south down the Smith Street corridor. EXCLUDED from this feature: that riverfront dock tail (1.1 mi) and the Smith Street corridor north of the yard (reversal to (-73.92241, 41.71093), 1.25 mi) - very probably dock/yard track (the New Haven bought the P&E in 1907 for its Poughkeepsie 'terminals and docks'). The drawn line starts at the south end of the Smith Street corridor beside the OSM 'Smith Street Yard Connector' / 'Poughkeepsie & Eastern Mainline' ways; that point is chosen because the trace from it fits Fowler's 21.3 mi to Stissing Jct, whereas starting at the reversal gives about 22.8 mi. The exact site of the passenger station ('west of Smith Street', Sanborn 1895 sheet 32 / Beers 1891) was NOT checked against those maps. Drawn on the P&E's OWN pre-1907 alignment (Smith Street - Van Wagner's - Pleasant Valley - Salt Point), not the later CNE 'via Stissing' route, which used the ex-P&C entry from Poughkeepsie to Salt Point; the two coincide only Salt Point - Stissing and for about 2.7 mi near Van Wagner's (roughly 1.9-4.6 mi out of the Smith Street start). Present-day OSM ways trace the abandoned grade as last used (CNE/NH era, to 1938); no relocation of the P&E's own line is known, but none was ruled out either. Commons map data: Data:Poughkeepsie and Eastern Railway.map, CC BY 4.0 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Data:Poughkeepsie_and_Eastern_Railway.map).

segments.note: Poughkeepsie (Smith Street) - Van Wagner's - Pleasant Valley - Salt Point - Clinton Corners - Upton Lake - Stanfordville - McIntyre - Stissing Junction (with the Dutchess & Columbia). Opened 24 Jan 1871 (WPE, WNDC, both citing Haight 1976). Stissing was 'the eastern terminus of the Poughkeepsie and Eastern Railroad' in Aug 1871 (Connecticut Western News 11 Aug 1871); 'several trains now pass daily' by Jan 1872 (CWN 5 Jan 1872); passenger trains Stissing - Poughkeepsie in 1872 (Bellows Falls Times 1 Mar 1872); a P&E conductor's 'passengers' in 1873 (CWN 12 Sep 1873). Receiver Jacob I. Carpenter from 24 Jun 1874 - the same company, not a split; 1874 is drawn by continuity under the receiver, confirmed working into Jan 1875 by the special train in the Stissing - State Line feature. Ends 1874 at year resolution: the line passed to the Poughkeepsie, Hartford and Boston on 15 May 1875 and 1875 is drawn on that company's feature. Headway is an ESTIMATE from 'several trains daily' (1872); not sourced as a figure.

Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Stissing Junction - Pine Plains over Dutchess & Columbia track by trackage rights (drawn on the D&C/ND&C geometry; the D&C's own trains are drawn there in central_new_england_railway.geojson), then the P&E's own line Pine Plains - Ancram Lead Mines - Halstead's - Tanner's - Boston Corners (Harlem crossing) - Mount Riga - State Line (Connecticut Western junction). Pine Plains - State Line opened 1 Oct 1872 (WPE, citing Haight); a Jan 1872 plan for State Line by 1 May with through trains to Hartford (CWN 26 Jan 1872) was a plan, not service. 1873: a carload of ministers bound for the Canaan camp meeting rode P&E trains through to State Line (CWN 12 Sep 1873). Late Jan 1875: 'a special train from Poughkeepsie' carried ~25 citizens to meet the Boston Board of Trade party 'at the New York state line' (CWN 29 Jan 1875) - a charter under the receiver, which shows the line working at the turn of 1874/75; 1875 itself is drawn on the PH&B feature. Receivership from 24 Jun 1874 is not a split. Headway is an ESTIMATE; not sourced.

segments.note: Poughkeepsie - Pleasant Valley - Salt Point - Stanfordville - Stissing - Pine Plains (D&C/ND&C trackage) - Ancram Lead Mines - Boston Corners. From 15 May 1875: 'the road is now run by the Poughkeepsie, Hartford and Boston railroad company' (Springfield Weekly Republican 21 May 1875). Dated passenger evidence: 1876 trains blocked by drifts near Boston Corners (Worcester Daily Spy 27 Mar 1876); Jan 1881 through trains stopped by snow and the road reopened (Democratic Advocate 15 and 29 Jan 1881; Independent Statesman 3 Feb 1881); 1882 the PH&B route 'carries more passengers in a day ...' (CWN 4 Jan 1882, quoting the Poughkeepsie Eagle); 1884 Russell's station in the 1884 Official Guide (FNY line 12) and chartered specials in Oct 1884 (NY Tribune 18 Oct 1884); Feb 1885 'the inward bound train ... at Boston Corners' (NY Tribune 17 Feb 1885). 1877-1880 and 1883 are interior years with no suggestion of suspension, drawn by continuity. The pre-1884 bankruptcy is not a split. Drawn to Boston Corners only: the PH&B's own trains on the Boston Corners - State Line leg are evidenced only in 1881 (separate feature), and that leg passed to the H&CW on 1 Apr 1884. END IS [OPEN]: 1885 is the last CONFIRMED PH&B passenger year, NOT a known end - the road was sold late in 1886 and the New York and Massachusetts took over on 22 Jan 1887; 1886 is withheld, not disproven. Do not extend without evidence. The NY&M era 1887-1892 is NOT drawn: no NY&M passenger year has been confirmed (a known gap, not an assertion that trains stopped). Headway is an ESTIMATE; not sourced.

segments.note: Boston Corners - Mount Riga - State Line, the P&E-built leg owned by the PH&B until the H&CW bought it (contract 26 Jan 1884, effective 1 Apr 1884 per WRC; 1 Sep per Robinson). [ANCHOR] 1881 is the single year with a PH&B train shown running to this end: 'For the first time since last Friday a train got through from Poughkeepsie to Millerton' (Independent Statesman 3 Feb 1881). ROUTE BY INFERENCE: Millerton is 1 mi west of State Line on the CW-leased D&C mile, and the only PH&B route to it is Boston Corners - Mount Riga - State Line; the alternative via the Harlem from Boston Corners would not be called the PH&B. That is an inference about the route, not a statement in the source. Service certainly ran wider both ways (the 1882 Eagle speaks of the PH&B route 'over the Connecticut Western'), but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor to 1875-1883 without evidence, and do not delete it to tidy the map. The Rhinebeck & Connecticut and H&CW also ran their own trains over this leg (drawn in central_new_england_railway.geojson). Headway is an ESTIMATE; not sourced.

segments.note: Poughkeepsie (Smith Street) - Pleasant Valley - Salt Point - Clinton Corners - Upton Lake - Stanfordville - Stissing - Pine Plains (ND&C trackage) - Ancram Lead Mines - Boston Corners. Poughkeepsie and Eastern RAILWAY, reorganized 13 Apr 1893 out of the New York and Massachusetts (WPE) - a different corporation from the 1871-1875 Poughkeepsie and Eastern RAILROAD sharing its display name and colour here. Evidence: 1893 Official Guide at every P&E station and a P&E public timetable of 1896 (FNY line 12, letters z and 'PE 1896t'); 1896 the train 'runs twice a day' (Rawlins Republican 8 May 1896, a humorous syndicated squib); Russell Sage's poor-children's specials to Upton Lake Park 1897-1900 (Topeka State Journal 18 Aug 1899; NY Tribune 17 Aug 1900) - charters, which Rule 1 counts; 1902 a MIXED train of four freight cars, a mail car and a coach near Boston Corners (Waterbury Democrat 9 Jul 1902); 12 Jul 1904 a P&E passenger train collided with a freight at Salt Point (Waterbury Evening Democrat 13 Jul 1904). Receivership from 17 Jun 1898 is the same company, not a split. END IS [OPEN]: 1904 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - nothing dated was found for 1905 to the 25 Jun 1907 merger into the Central New England (NH-owned from early 1907); those years are withheld, not disproven. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an ESTIMATE from 'twice a day' (1896); not sourced as a figure.
